name: photonsmith
description: A pbrt-v4-style physically based renderer with CPU, OptiX (NVIDIA) and Metal (macOS) backends, plus BDPT, MLT and SPPM, tested against closed-form results.

paragraphs: (formerly raytracer: the repository was renamed; old links redirect. The programs keep their names: raytracer, RayTracerGUI.)

An open-source, pbrt-v4-compatible path tracer for the CPU, NVIDIA OptiX (Windows) and Apple Metal (macOS), with a Qt GUI, a Scene Builder and a Live Preview you can drag objects around in. It reads pbrt-v4 scene files, and its renders are checked against closed-form results, not only against each other.

A physically-based renderer with parallel CPU, GPU (OptiX) (Windows + NVIDIA) and GPU (Metal) (macOS) implementations, built up from the "Ray Tracing in One Weekend" book series into a much broader pbrt-v4-style feature set: 168 built-in scenes and 66 test scenes, a wide material library, multiple light types, real triangle-mesh/texture support, BVH acceleration, volumetrics, and an experimental SPPM (photon-mapping) integrator alongside standard path tracing.
features: ✅ Path tracing with next-event estimation and multiple importance sampling (power heuristic)
✅ BVH acceleration on both CPU and GPU (SAH-based CPU BVH; OptiX's native BVH/GAS on GPU) — not a linear scan

✅ 168 built-in scenes and 66 test scenes (each has a stable name such as cornell-box, and a short id such as A1) spanning the "Ray Tracing" book series, a pbrt-v4-style material/light/camera showcase, dozens of…
✅ Real triangle meshes: OBJ loading with BVH, per-face .mtl materials, and real mapKd image-texture sampling (not just flat colors) on both CPU and GPU

✅ Stochastic Progressive Photon Mapping (SPPM), an alternative integrator for hard caustic/glass scenes a standard path tracer struggles to converge — on the CPU, and on the GPU for sphere/quad scenes (see Known…
